Flight Software Platform Engineer
Req #528
Greenwood Village, CO, 6060 South Willow Drive, Greenwood Village, Colorado, United States of America
Apply
Share
Job Description
Posted Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 6:00 AM

York Space Systems was founded to radically improve spacecraft affordability and reliability, transforming, and enabling next- generation space mission operations worldwide. Today, York is one of the most innovative aerospace companies, specializing in end-to-end customer solutions and the rapid production of spacecraft platforms. York’s complete Space Segment Solution includes spacecraft production, payload integration, system integration & test, launch services, ground segment services, and mission operations, enabling customers to leverage York’s existing technology solutions to get to orbit rapidly and responsively. We’re looking to expand our team across the board.

York is seeking a Junior / Early Career Flight Software Platform Engineer to support the Flight Software Engineering team. 

This role is intended for an engineer early in their career who is interested in embedded Linux, spacecraft systems, mission-critical software, and hands-on platform development. The Platform Team owns the operating system foundation used to deliver embedded flight software for space applications. 

The ideal candidate is curious, technically motivated, and excited to learn Linux platform development, embedded software practices, hardware/software integration, and flight software delivery in a fast-moving aerospace environment. 

This is a hands-on engineering role with mentorship from senior engineers and technical leads. Over time, this engineer will grow ownership in embedded Linux platform components, integration workflows, test automation, and software release support. 

 

Responsibilities:

Participate in an agile scrum team focused on supporting the embedded Linux platform used to deliver flight software for space applications. 
Support development and maintenance of the embedded Linux platform, including: 
Linux kernel configuration and debugging 
Bootloader and BSP support 
Root filesystem updates 
Core system services and systemd configuration 
Device driver integration and troubleshooting 
Platform scripts, tools, and configuration files 
Embedded Linux interfaces and processes 
Collaborate with team members, management, systems engineers, hardware teams, application teams, and mission operations to support project execution. 
Assist with understanding and expanding requirements based on high-level specifications, system needs, and mission use cases. 
Contribute to platform stability, security, and maintainability by: 
Investigating bugs and integration issues 
Supporting software updates and release activities 
Helping maintain reproducible builds 
Documenting changes, assumptions, and troubleshooting steps 
Identifying risks and raising issues early 
Communicating challenges, failures, and successes clearly 
Participate in technical design reviews and code reviews to improve quality and maintainability of deliverables. 
Support implementation of software architectures and designs that meet requirements. 
Develop code following project coding guidelines, process requirements, and review expectations. 
Assist with unit, integration, software-in-the-loop, and hardware-in-the-loop testing, including: 
Developing and executing unit tests 
Verifying requirements and interface behavior 
Supporting code coverage activities 
Helping analyze test results 
Supporting SITL and HITL integration and testing 
Capturing test results and release artifacts 
Work with other subsystems to support proper integration of platform software into the broader flight software design. 
Participate in implementation approach discussions by helping evaluate cost, complexity, schedule, and technical risk. 
Support continuous improvement of team practices, including: 
Improving documentation and knowledge sharing 
Automating repetitive development or test tasks 
Contributing to CI/CD improvements 
Participating in retrospectives and post-release reviews 
Helping improve release confidence and integration quality 
Grow technical ownership over time in areas such as: 
Yocto-based build systems 
Linux kernel customization 
Device trees and low-level hardware interfaces 
Embedded networking concepts 
Platform test automation 
Flight software deployment and update flows 
Software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop environments 

 

Required Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience 
0–3 years of experience in software development, embedded systems, Linux, or related areas 
Basic programming experience in one or more of: 
C , C++ , Python, Bash / shell scripting 
Familiarity with Linux development environments 
Interest in embedded Linux, spacecraft systems, or mission-critical software 
Familiarity with basic software development practices, including Git, code reviews, debugging, and documentation 
Ability to troubleshoot technical issues with support from senior engineers 
Willingness to learn complex systems and ask good questions 
Ability to communicate technical challenges, risks, and progress clearly 
Strong teamwork and collaboration skills 
Ability to work in a cross-functional engineering environment 
Love Space! 
Willingness to work full-time in our Greenwood Village, CO office

 

Preferred Qualifications 

Internship, academic, hobbyist, or project experience with Linux or embedded systems 
Exposure to Linux internals, bootloaders, kernels, device trees, or root filesystems 
Exposure to Yocto, Buildroot, or other embedded Linux build systems 
Exposure to cross-compilation and low-level system interaction 
Familiarity with device drivers or hardware/software interfaces 
Familiarity with networking concepts and protocols 
Experience with GitLab, CI/CD, issue tracking tools, or automated test pipelines 
Experience with hardware bring-up, lab equipment, or debugging on target hardware 
Familiarity with unit testing, integration testing, SITL, or HITL testing 
Interest in aerospace, spacecraft operations, or operational software systems 
Hobbyist project experience using Linux, embedded boards, robotics, radios, or home lab environments 
Ability to obtain or maintain a US Secret Clearance 

 

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required.  Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, skill set, experience, and/or performance.  

 

Benefits

100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance (subject to spousal surcharge).
Company holidays, floating holidays, and sick time.
Unlimited PTO.
Generous 401(k) match.

How To Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by clicking the “Apply” link at the top of the page. York Space Systems will be accepting applications on a rolling basis until the position is closed. York Space Systems provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, military or protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.  Must have permanent authorization to work in the United States.  This policy applies to all terms and conditions or employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.  YORK SPACE SYSTEMS IS AN EEO EMPLOYER.
